item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01015","case1_error":"Reverses the twice-as-many relationship, multiplying Emmy’s remaining eight by two instead of dividing to find Rosa’s count.","case2_error":"Divides the area into six equal shares despite the living room’s triple size; the apartment contains eight ordinary-room shares.","reason":"The first reverses a multiplicative comparison; the second uses an incorrect denominator when allocating a total among unequal rooms.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01016","case1_error":"Uses the original nine T-shirts as the tripling base instead of the three sweaters found.","case2_error":"Computes remaining washers as used minus purchased, reversing subtraction; the closing sentence contradicts that erroneous derivation.","reason":"The first selects the wrong comparison base; the second reverses the inventory subtraction. Its error is explicitly shown, beyond an answer-marker conflict.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01017","case1_error":"Equates current practice with past half-practice, asserting P = P/2 and P = 2P, then unjustifiably concludes two days.","case2_error":"Instructs subtracting the repair expense twice and supplies 1100 without any calculation supporting it.","reason":"The first introduces false temporal equalities; the second duplicates an expense deduction and gives an unsupported final number.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01018","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written subtraction 48 − 17 − 10 as 11 instead of 21.","case2_error":"Subtracts the production cost of only one necklace from revenue for thirty necklaces.","reason":"The first is numerical evaluation of a correct expression; the second fails to scale costs to the quantity sold.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01019","case1_error":"Invents an initial inventory of zero and uses inconsistent inventory updates, ignoring the two returned cookies.","case2_error":"Gives 52 after correctly specifying 8 × 7 − 2, with no shown evaluation supporting that answer.","reason":"The first fabricates an inventory and mishandles its changes; the second supplies an unsupported final number after a correct formula.","judgment":"different"}]}
